knowledge-base.overview: WordPress 6.0+ guardrails, patterns, and best practices for plugin and theme development. Covers plugin architecture, hooks and filters, the REST API with WP_REST_Controller, Block Editor (Gutenberg) block registration, security (nonces, capability checks, escaping, sanitization), WP_Query, WP-CLI commands, and coding standards. Applies to PHP 8.0+ WordPress projects.

core-principles.principle: All customization goes through actions and filters — never modify core files. Every plugin entry point is a hook callback.
Escape all output, sanitize all input, verify nonces on every form and AJAX handler, check capabilities before every privileged action.
Every PHP file that is not a template must guard against direct access with if (!defined('ABSPATH')) { exit; }
Use $wpdb->prepare() for every custom database query. Never concatenate user input into SQL strings.
New UI functionality uses Gutenberg blocks with block.json, server-side rendering for dynamic content, and @wordpress/* packages for the editor.

guardrail.rule: Use $wpdb->prepare() for ALL custom database queries. Never concatenate user data into SQL.
Verify nonces on every form submission and AJAX handler. Use wp_verify_nonce() for forms and check_ajax_referer() for AJAX.
Check capabilities before every privileged action with current_user_can(). Never assume the current user has permissions.
Escape all output in the correct context. Use esc_html() for text, esc_attr() for attributes, esc_url() for URLs, wp_kses_post() for allowed HTML.
Prevent direct file access in every PHP file that is not a template: if (!defined('ABSPATH')) { exit; }
Never use query_posts(). Use WP_Query or get_posts() instead. query_posts() corrupts the main loop and causes pagination bugs.
Never hardcode URLs. Use home_url(), admin_url(), plugin_dir_url(__FILE__), and get_template_directory_uri() for all URL generation.
Register all scripts and styles through wp_enqueue_scripts (frontend) and admin_enqueue_scripts (admin) hooks. Never echo script tags directly.
Always define permission_callback on REST API endpoints. Use __return_true only for genuinely public endpoints. Return WP_Error for error responses.
Use namespaces for all plugin/theme classes and require vendor/autoload.php. Use text domains and __() / _e() for all user-facing strings.

pattern.name: Main Plugin File and Bootstrap
pattern.description: Plugin header, constants, autoload, activation/deactivation hooks, and lazy init via plugins_loaded.
pattern.example:
<?php
/**
 * Plugin Name: My Plugin
 * Plugin URI:  https://example.com/my-plugin
 * Description: A modern WordPress plugin
 * Version:     1.0.0
 * Requires at least: 6.0
 * Requires PHP:      8.0
 * Author:      Your Name
 * Text Domain: my-plugin
 * Domain Path: /languages
 */

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MyPlugin;

if (!defined('ABSPATH')) { exit; }

define('MY_PLUGIN_VERSION',  '1.0.0');
define('MY_PLUGIN_PATH',     plugin_dir_path(__FILE__));
define('MY_PLUGIN_URL',      plugin_dir_url(__FILE__));
define('MY_PLUGIN_BASENAME', plugin_basename(__FILE__));

require_once MY_PLUGIN_PATH . 'vendor/autoload.php';

register_activation_hook(__FILE__,   [Activator::class,  'activate']);
register_deactivation_hook(__FILE__, [Deactivator::class, 'deactivate']);

add_action('plugins_loaded', function (): void {
    Plugin::getInstance()->init();
});

pattern.name: Singleton Plugin Class
pattern.description: Thread-safe singleton that initialises subsystems on plugins_loaded.
pattern.example:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MyPlugin;

final class Plugin
{
    private static ?self $instance = null;

    public static function getInstance(): self
    {
        if (self::$instance === null) {
            self::$instance = new self();
        }
        return self::$instance;
    }

    private function __construct() {}

    public function init(): void
    {
        load_plugin_textdomain('my-plugin', false, dirname(MY_PLUGIN_BASENAME) . '/languages');

        if (is_admin()) {
            new Admin\Admin();
        }

        new Frontend\Frontend();
        new Api\RestApi();
        new Blocks\BlockManager();
    }
}

pattern.name: REST API Controller
pattern.description: WP_REST_Controller subclass with namespace versioning, permission callbacks, and pagination headers.
pattern.example:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MyPlugin\Api;

use WP_REST_Controller;
use WP_REST_Request;
use WP_REST_Response;
use WP_REST_Server;

final class BooksController extends WP_REST_Controller
{
    protected $namespace = 'my-plugin/v1';
    protected $rest_base = 'books';

    public function registerRoutes(): void
    {
        register_rest_route($this->namespace, '/' . $this->rest_base, [
            [
                'methods'             => WP_REST_Server::READABLE,
                'callback'            => [$this, 'getItems'],
                'permission_callback' => [$this, 'getItemsPermissions'],
                'args'                => $this->getCollectionParams(),
            ],
            [
                'methods'             => WP_REST_Server::CREATABLE,
                'callback'            => [$this, 'createItem'],
                'permission_callback' => [$this, 'createItemPermissions'],
            ],
        ]);
    }

    public function getItems(WP_REST_Request $request): WP_REST_Response
    {
        $query = new \WP_Query([
            'post_type'      => 'book',
            'posts_per_page' => $request->get_param('per_page') ?? 10,
            'paged'          => $request->get_param('page') ?? 1,
        ]);

        $items    = array_map(fn($post) => $this->formatItem($post), $query->posts);
        $response = new WP_REST_Response($items, 200);
        $response->header('X-WP-Total',      $query->found_posts);
        $response->header('X-WP-TotalPages', $query->max_num_pages);

        return $response;
    }

    public function getItemsPermissions(): bool   { return true; }
    public function createItemPermissions(): bool  { return current_user_can('publish_posts'); }
}

esc_html / esc_attr / esc_url / wp_kses_post for each context
